newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares retreat as investors book profits.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares retreat as investors book profits.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed lower in volatile trade on Wednesday as speculators and institutional investors pocketed profits after a recent rise in prices, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index ended 9.65 points lower at 827.40.

"The fall in share prices during the day was a technical correction which was overdue as the index had jumped by nearly 12 percent since the presentation of the financial budget," said Shree Bhagwan Garg of brokers Means Leasing.

Delhi shares had surged by more than 12 percent since Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced tax cuts and other measures considered friendly to stock market investors last Friday in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget.
"Sizeable selling by domestic financial institutions disrupted the bull run in share prices," said another broker.
Reliance Industries closed 11.80 rupees lower at 303.05 on sustained selling by domestic financial institutions and speculators, brokers said.
Bajaj Auto drifted 10.50 rupees lower to 1,086.
State Bank of India slipped 6.55 rupees to 327.45.
However, ACC bucked the trend to close 14 rupees higher at 1,800 on buying by foreign institutional investors.
